# DevCult

> DevCult is a DevEx consultancy for blockchain ecosystems. We run hackathons, fix onboarding, and build DevRel programs that produce measurable developer adoption.

We fix what turns developers away from blockchains. Most ecosystems lose developers in the first 30 minutes — broken tutorials, confusing architecture, documentation written for people who already understand the system. We've seen it everywhere. We fix it.

## Services

- [Developer Onboarding Optimization](https://devcult.io/about#onboarding): Audit developer journeys from landing page to first API call. Time-to-Hello-World analysis, error message archaeology, cognitive load reduction, environment setup elimination.

- [Technical Documentation Audits](https://devcult.io/about#documentation): Systematic audits that surface accuracy decay, discovery failures, maintainability gaps, and AI-readability issues. Prioritized fix lists with estimated impact.

- [Hackathon Operations](https://devcult.io/about#hackathons): End-to-end hackathon design and execution. Pre-event activation, on-site technical support, Project Clinic workshops, real-time feedback loops, post-event reporting with actual metrics.

- [Post-Hackathon Support](https://devcult.io/about#incubation): Team incubation programs that turn weekend projects into production deployments. Technical viability assessment, architecture guidance, ecosystem integration, grant/funding preparation.

- [Ecosystem DevRel Strategy](https://devcult.io/about#devrel-strategy): DevRel programs with measurable outcomes — developer activation, retention metrics, community health indicators. Coordination across teams, governance mechanisms.

- [Blockchain Education & Consulting](https://devcult.io/about#education): Technical workshops on smart contract development, runtime architecture, data indexing, AI agent integration. Ecosystem strategy consulting.

## Proof of Work

- ETHBelgrade 2025: 25.6% of all submissions, 11 prizes, 2 of 5 main track winners, 133 new community members
- ETHRome 2025: 17.5% of submissions, 9 prizes, 109 new community members, 7 post-hackathon leads
